frame_front_clamp.title: Braced frame and front clamp
frame_front_clamp.description: Split clamp for the Ø44 mm microscope, captured vertical dovetail guide, NEMA17 mounting plate, and two triangulated struts with depth gussets.

rear_clamp.title: Rear microscope clamp
rear_clamp.description: Rear half of the split microscope clamp. Two M5 bolts join the clamp halves; the nominal bore is 44.4 mm.

front_axle_bridge.title: Front axle bridge
front_axle_bridge.description: Second support for the wheel axle, with two arms carrying loads back to the braced frame. The bridge clears the moving rod and crank hardware.

sector_crank.title: Internal sector crank
sector_crank.description: 136 mm crank wheel with a 180° slot, 60 internal teeth on a virtual 120-tooth ring, and a 25 mm crank radius.

motor_pinion.title: NEMA17 drive pinion
motor_pinion.description: 20-tooth module 1 pinion, 20° pressure angle, with a 5 mm D-shaft bore and radial retention hole. It drives against the teeth inside the sector slot.

connecting_rod.title: Connecting rod
connecting_rod.description: 110 mm pivot spacing. Two 625ZZ bearings connect the crank to the vertically moving carriage.

probe_carriage.title: External angled probe carriage
probe_carriage.description: Captured vertical dovetail carriage and gusseted arm with an external split 6 mm collet. The probe axis stays 60° above the specimen plate while the carriage moves 40 mm vertically.

microscope_reference.title: Microscope cylinder reference
microscope_reference.description: Ø44 mm microscope envelope with its lower end at world Y=0. The body length is an illustrative reference; check the actual objective envelope.

probe_reference.title: Necked metal probe reference
probe_reference.description: Custom 104 mm metal probe reference: pointed tip and 1 mm stem over the first 60 mm, a 10 mm taper, and a 6 mm shank from 70–104 mm. The 6 mm shank is held outside the projected optical field.

specimen_plate_reference.title: Specimen plate reference
specimen_plate_reference.description: Horizontal plate 100 mm below the microscope end. The lowered probe tip touches the center of the plate.

notes.fit: End mount for a Ø44 mm microscope cylinder, with a nominal 44.4 mm split-clamp bore and a 100 mm working distance to the specimen. The carriage moves 40 mm straight vertically; the externally held probe remains 60° above the plate. A custom necked metal probe has a 1 mm stem in the central field and a 6 mm shank in the external collet. Confirm the actual objective envelope and optical field.
notes.validation: All 48 exported components are valid single solids and passed STEP roundtrip checks. No intersections at 41 checked poses; Ø44 projected optical field clear of printed parts. Every component pair was checked at each pose (1128 pairs per pose), with no excluded parts or regions. A conservative full-length Ø6 mm probe envelope was also checked against every other component, replacing the necked probe reference. This is a geometry and motion prototype; stiffness, strength, backlash, fit tolerances and manufacturing need physical validation. These sampled checks do not prove clearance at every intermediate position. Separate conservative bounds keep every printed part outside the Ø44 projected barrel corridor throughout the prescribed vertical stroke, with the bounds checked against a 24 mm corridor radius. The projected footprint is not a measured lens field of view. The checked minimum gap between a full-length Ø6 mm probe envelope and the front clamp is 1.885 mm.
notes.exports: STEP is available for all 48 displayed components and the complete assembly. Genuine Parasolid x_t export is unavailable because no licensed writer is installed. Import STEP into a CAD tool with a Parasolid exporter to produce x_t. The complete bundle includes build123d source, requirements, all component STEP files, seven printable-part STLs, assembly STEP/GLB, viewer geometry, dimensions, manifests, checksums and verification reports. CAD downloads share the lowered contact-pose assembly placement; arrange STL orientations in your slicer.
